report.summary: An automated configuration sync reduced the maximum database connection pool size in ledger-service from 50 to 5, leading to connection timeouts and error rate spikes in both ledger-service and payments-api.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Automated config change drastically reduced database pool size in ledger-service

supporting.note: Config change reduced db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 at 13:12.
Ledger service error rate spiked upward at 13:15.
Ledger service p99 latency spiked starting at 13:14.
HikariPool errors show total=5 and active=5 with request timeouts starting at 13:15.
Payments-api received 503 errors when calling ledger-service starting at 13:15.
RPS remained at normal baseline levels.

contradicting.note: RPS showed no abnormal surge during the incident window.

facts.text: At 2026-10-06T13:12:00+00:00, config change chg-8919 normalized db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 on ledger-service.
Error rates for both payments-api and ledger-service started increasing at 13:15.
HikariPool errors reported connection timeouts with total=5 active=5.

assumptions: The configuration change chg-8919 was applied universally by platform-bot and incorrectly clamped the connection pool for ledger-service.

timeline.event: Config change chg-8919 applied to ledger-service reducing db.pool.max_size to 5.
Error rate anomaly begins on payments-api and ledger-service.
First payments-api error logged for ledger-service connection failure.

recommended_actions.action: Revert configuration change chg-8919 to restore ledger-service database connection pool size back to 50.
recommended_actions.rationale: Directly resolves the resource constraint causing connection timeouts and payment confirmation failures.

recommended_actions.action: Add validation checks and guardrails to platform-bot configuration syncs.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents automated config scripts from applying dangerously low pool size limits to backend services.
